title: feat: allow to put notes in namespaces on classDiagram
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

It improve its support for notes inside namespaces.

Resolves #4706

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00e9bc5c-8935-42a0-804e-92dd3aea0df5)


## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

It allows NoteNode to be added in the namespace.

- `classStatements` parses not only `classStatement` but also `noteStatement` and returns an array of their IDs.
- `addClassesToNamespace()` takes a new param `noteNames` and associates the namespace with the note.
- In `classRender-v2.ts` `addNotes()` implements the process of adding to namespace like `addClasses()`.
- Changed `notes` from `Array` to `ClassNoteMap`.
- Add fields to `ClassNote`.
  - parent: keeps the ID of the namespace.
  - index: holds the number of the note. index: holds the number of the note (used as a reference when generating the edge ID)

author: kairi003

comments.author: jgreywolf
comments.body: Can you help me understand this change? What do the extra array definitions do?

comments.author: kairi003
comments.body:
Thank you for the review!

In short, this is to pass not only class node identifiers but also note node identifiers to `yy.addClassesToNamespace()`.

`classStatements` is an array of identifiers for class nodes within the namespace.

Originally, only regular class nodes were stored in this array. These were passed to `yy.addClassesToNamespace()` within `namespaceStatement`, linking them to the namespace.

My change extends the format of `classStatements` from `[classIdentifiers]` to `[[classIdentifiers], [noteIdentifiers]]`. This allows note node identifiers to be passed to `yy.addClassesToNamespace()` and linked to the namespace.

comments.author: kairi003
comments.body:
Of course, for better extensibility and readability, we could use an object (associative array) instead of an array, like this:
```
classStatement NEWLINE                   {$$={classNames: [$1], noteNames: []}
...
```
However, I thought it might be overkill to do so just for the two types: class nodes and note nodes.

comments.author: kairi003
comments.body: Which do you think is better? I don’t have strong feelings about it, so I can rewrite it quickly.

comments.body: The way you have done it is fine, it just took your explanation to help me see it :)
